- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to capture mean reversion.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7) and history shows volatility, model tends to lag; add 1–3 days of lagged price movement to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true mean; apply a 1–3% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 2+ consecutive bearish → bullish), model may misread trend; use sentiment-weighted average of last 5–7 days for correction.
